label: unnumbered (table: Urgent Policy Priorities for a Prosperous Kenya)
title: Urgent Policy Priorities for a Prosperous Kenya
chart_type: table, 2 columns (Economic constraint | Urgent Policy Priorities) with bullet lists; starts on PDF p.8 and continues on PDF p.9; two decorative icons above the column headers
indicators: Fiscal constraint: enhance efficiency and equity of the tax system; improve expenditure efficiency and equity; improve transparency and accountability of public spending; strengthen governance and accountability to contain corruption

External constraint: implement trade agreements (AfCFTA, AGOA, EU-EPA); align domestic regulations with international standards, especially environmental standards; boost FDI and investment promotion (systemic support to investors, open domestic sectors to FDI, implement international investment protocols, foster the role of KenInvest)

Productivity constraint: national and sub-national licensing (address economy-wide and sectoral regulatory inefficiencies, align county licensing procedures to avoid fragmentation); reduce barriers to competition in key sectors, including where enterprises with State shareholding operate; increase access to affordable infrastructure services and improve infrastructure management; enhance equity and quality in basic and tertiary education, and boost innovation

Climate constraint: enhance water productivity of existing rainfed cropping systems and sustain water resources in landscapes; explore concessional green financing (credit-enhanced sovereign green or sustainability-linked financing, SLF); leverage natural capital (conservation, ecotourism) [p.9]; multifaceted approach to the green transition: renewable energy, green transport, logistics operations, digital comparative advantage [p.9]
source_note: No source line printed
method: Qualitative summary of policy recommendations; no data
replication_notes: Text table only. A table or text-rendering tool can reproduce it from the transcribed content. No data is needed. Continues on PDF p.9 (printed p.6) with the last two climate bullets.
key_values: 4 constraint rows: Fiscal, External, Productivity, Climate
Fiscal 4 bullets, External 3, Productivity 4, Climate 4 (2 on p.8, 2 on p.9)

label: unnumbered (policy framework diagram)
title: A policy framework to rebalancing and reinvigorating economic growth in Kenya
chart_type: conceptual network diagram: 4 coloured boxes linked by labelled two-way arrows, outer arcs, and a brace underneath labelled as the foundation
indicators: Nodes: Fiscal Space (orange), Productivity Growth (teal), Climate Resilience (green), International Integration (purple); foundation: 'Transparent and efficient public institutions'
Fiscal Space -> Productivity Growth: 'Efficient public investment expands the PPF and finances productivity-enhancing enablers'
Productivity Growth -> Fiscal Space: 'Raises more fiscal revenues from productive firms'
Fiscal Space -> Climate Resilience: 'Increases resources for mitigation and adaptation'
Climate Resilience -> Fiscal Space: 'Reduces likelihood of unplanned spending pressures and revenue shortfalls'
Fiscal Space -> International Integration: 'Enables undistorted interest and exchange rates'
International Integration -> Fiscal Space: 'Creates FX flow to fund investments and pay for external liabilities'
International Integration -> Productivity Growth: 'Promotes competition and enables the transmission of knowhow through efficiency-seeking FDI and imports'
Productivity Growth -> International Integration: 'Raises exports due to more productive firms'
Climate Resilience -> International Integration: 'FX climate finance funds external accounts'
International Integration -> Climate Resilience: 'Brings inputs for resilience and mitigation'
Top outer arc: 'Builds resilience to shocks from firms and households'; bottom outer arc: 'Reduces volatility and limits destruction of capital'

method: Conceptual framework; no data

label: Figure 2
section: 2 Growth drivers during the last 20 years
title: Contributions to real value-added growth* (shared headline with Figure 3: Kenya's economic growth has been driven by the constant expansion of the services sector, at the same time the government sector expanded, and exports withdrew)
chart_type: stacked bar chart by period, with positive and negative stacks
indicators: Contribution to real value-added growth, percentage points, by sector: Agriculture, Manufacturing, Construction, Rest of industry, Services, FISM (financial intermediation services indirectly measured)
Period average total growth g shown in the category labels (%)
source_note: Source: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, 2025. *Note: The growth decomposition is an approximation and individual growth rates may not add up to the total growth rate. Sectoral and expenditure growth rates are weighted by their average share in total value-added or GDP during the period. Exports and imports data is shown until 2023 and do not reflect revisions made in the Kenya Economic Survey 2025.
data_sources: KNBS Economic Survey (national accounts, GDP by activity at constant prices)
method: Approximate sectoral growth decomposition: contribution = sector's average real growth over the period x its average share in total value added over the period
replication_notes: Needs KNBS real value added by ISIC sector, 2001–2024 (Economic Survey or Statistical Abstract), with sectors grouped into agriculture, manufacturing, construction, rest of industry (mining, electricity, water), services and FISM. Average annual growth for each sector is multiplied by its average share in the period. Splicing across KNBS base revisions may be needed for 2001–2010. The y-axis runs -1 to 6 and is labelled 'Percentage points'. In the 2020 bar the readable stacks net to about +1.2 pp, but the label says g = 0.5%. Matching that label exactly may need the authors' exact vintage.

label: Figure 35

source_note: Sources: Own calculations based on ILO Modelled Projections (Nov. 2023; https://ilostat.ilo.org/data/) and KNSO. *Note: For further details on the methodology to decompose value-added per worker, please see McMillan and Rodrik (2011) and de Vries, Timmer, and de Vries (2015).
data_sources: KNBS (printed as 'KNSO') national accounts value added
method: Shift-share decomposition of labor productivity (value added per worker) growth into within-sector and between-sector (structural change / inter-sectoral reallocation) components by 3 broad sectors (McMillan and Rodrik 2011; de Vries, Timmer and de Vries 2015)
replication_notes: Needs real value added by sector (agriculture, industry, services) from KNBS, or WDI as a substitute, plus ILO modelled employment by the same sectors for 2011 and 2019. The page does not say whether the 1.8% is annualized or cumulative, nor which base-year weights are used. Text says inter-sectoral services is about 85% of the total.
